intended_object: The finitary symmetric group FSym(ι): the subgroup of Sym(ι) made of the permutations that move only finitely many points. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The carrier is {π | (fixedBy ι π)ᶜ.Finite}. Here (fixedBy ι π)ᶜ is the set of points that π moves, so the carrier is exactly the set of permutations with finite support. The definition works for an arbitrary type `ι` with no extra hypotheses, which is the natural generality. The closure proofs are standard: the support of a product lies in the union of the supports, and a permutation and its inverse have the same support.

When ι is finite, every permutation lies in this subgroup, as the docstring says. When ι is empty, Perm ι is trivial and the subgroup is the whole (trivial) group, which is also correct.

Mathlib uses the same predicate in `Equiv.Perm.mem_closure_isSwap`: a permutation is in the closure of the swaps exactly when its moved set is finite. That gives the docstring's description as the group generated by transpositions. However, Mathlib has no named definition of this subgroup, so there is no counterpart to cite.
